name: Mind
vision_statement: Every step of a person's request acts on everything the request has established so far, so a reply rests on the work done for it and the person can follow that work, at the cost of the fast tier.
opportunities: The loop's prompt can be rebuilt for each step from a template, cached head and context layers, the newest observations in full and older ones in one line, so a step's input stays small while the final answer still sees everything. That opens questions the parent solution does not ask: how much of the earlier steps a planner must see to keep continuity (from the second step the selected arm replaces the transcript with a short note that refers to step one, and its continuity is unmeasured), how a person is kept informed while a turn works (a first line, interim replies, the trail of what was done) without paying a model call for every line, and how a request that worked before skips the loop by replaying its known steps.
solution_coherence: Mind lets one step of a request build on the steps before it, and its rebuilt_per_step arm is made of the parts of one step. Budgeted prompt assembler writes the prompt a step sends within a size budget. Cost-ordered model tier selector with outage and allowance recovery picks the model tier a step starts on. Grounded chat turn handler turns the step's decision into the reply to a chat message. First-beat narration writes the first line a person reads while the turn works. How-I-got-this explanation writes, when the person asks for it, how the answer was reached, once the answer is out. Learned-operation fast path answers a request that worked before by replaying its known steps. Core ML tasks classifies the message a step is about. Whole-path answer check proves that a message is handled right across the whole path, with the first line that First-beat narration writes in it. It also proves the account of how the answer was reached, which How-I-got-this explanation writes on request. Reply in steps when the goal is not met yet decides when a turn that is not finished sends an interim message and what that message holds. Show the AI's work and next steps lays out the trail of the work a turn did. Mode-aware progress surfacing streams each event at the level the person wants.
